title: Notable recent biology and biomedical papers from the 2026-11-16 arXiv announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This relevance-ranked shortlist is inferred from checkable evidence in an incomplete biomedical corpus; it is not a popularity ranking, systematic review, or clinical evidence assessment. Much clinical and experimental biology research appears on bioRxiv or medRxiv instead.

sections.title: Daily biology and biomedical batch: 7 notable papers
sections.summary: The Monday, 16 November 2026 batch is dominated by function-aware protein evaluation and molecular modeling, alongside gene-response prediction and one MRI reconstruction study. Attention evidence is sparse, so entries are relevance-ranked, not measured hottest papers.

sections.title: Confident and Wrong: Structure Confidence Is a Poor Selection Filter for Protein Function
sections.abstract: The authors compare three lanmodulin design strategies and report that function-guided selection yielded substantially more terbium-binding variants than selection by structural-confidence scores.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 83.3% terbium binding in the function-guided panel versus 16.7% in the structure-confidence-selected panel, and argue that measured-function supervision is a better selection signal in this design setting.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison is bounded to lanmodulin rare-earth binding and three design strategies; it does not establish that structural confidence is unhelpful for all proteins or design tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New q-bio.BM submission; biochemical screening of 297 designs against terbium and dysprosium is a direct functional assay. No independent attention signal surfaced in targeted searches.

sections.title: CARVE: A glycan-specific framework for assessing protein-glycan binding-pose quality
sections.abstract: CARVE combines glycan-aware geometry and contact measures to classify predicted protein–glycan poses, then benchmarks nine methods on experimentally determined complexes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that HADDOCK3 had the highest acceptable-level success rate among the top 25 predictions per target (47%); no tested method exceeded 20% for high-quality, structurally valid poses.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a structural benchmark on existing complexes, not prospective experimental validation of new glycan binding. Temporal splitting reduces but cannot guarantee absence of training overlap for every prediction method.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New q-bio.BM submission; CARVE-Score reproduced quality classes on 25,068 poses (macro-F1 0.892), and CARVE-Bench covers 1,974 complexes and nine methods.

sections.title: Learning Task-Specific Antibody Representations via Function-Aware Masking
sections.abstract: The authors train antibody language models with function-aligned masking patterns and report improvements on the downstream tasks targeted by those patterns.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report gains of up to 14% on structure-related tasks and 5.9-fold on CDR-related tasks, using specialist and hybrid masking strategies.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluations use a medium-sized, approximately 38M-parameter model and computational benchmarks; label quality, model scale, and manually chosen hybrid mixtures remain limitations. No wet-lab binding gain is established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Listed as a replacement in today's q-bio.BM batch; the arXiv comment reports acceptance to MLCB 2026 (Oral), a checkable venue signal rather than a readership claim.

sections.title: S1Pert: Scalable Target-Specific Gene Response Prediction with System-One Intelligence
sections.abstract: S1Pert combines uncertainty-aware response labels, cached foundation-model representations, and a hierarchical decoder to predict gene-response direction for unseen genetic perturbations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report Macro-F1 gains of 5.8–6.4 percentage points over the strongest baseline across four evaluated cell-line datasets, with improved discrimination of target-specific response directions.
sections.unique_caveat: This is retrospective computational evaluation on existing perturbation data, not prospective CRISPR validation. Performance and response labels are benchmark- and cell-context-dependent.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New genomics submission; target-held-out evaluation in HepG2, Jurkat, RPE1, and K562, plus public code. No independent attention signal surfaced in targeted searches.

sections.title: Scan-specific k-space interpolation using deep Koopman autoencoders
sections.abstract: A scan-specific deep Koopman autoencoder reconstructs retrospectively undersampled brain MRI k-space data and is compared with GRAPPA and RAKI.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved reconstruction metrics over GRAPPA and RAKI and reader preference over RAKI in 38 of 52 cases, with better ratings for sharpness, aliasing, and overall image quality.
sections.unique_caveat: Data are retrospective brain scans from one dataset, not prospective patient scans or a multi-site evaluation. Reader-study preference is not clinical-outcome evidence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New medical-physics submission; 281 retrospectively undersampled brain MRI datasets and a 52-image reader study. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations at this snapshot.

sections.title: Exact stochastic theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation mediated by RNA-binding proteins
sections.abstract: An analytical stochastic model derives protein-number and burst-size distributions for RNA-binding-protein-mediated feedback and compares its predicted noise and rhythm transmission with transcriptional feedback.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author derives a steady-state distribution and sub-Poissonian criterion, and predicts that negative feedback favors post-transcriptional control for noise suppression and rhythm transmission, while positive feedback favors transcriptional control.
sections.unique_caveat: The results are theoretical predictions from a reaction model, not newly measured molecular or cellular effects; experimental tests are needed to assess assumptions and the predicted regime reversal.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New q-bio.MN submission, cross-listed in biological physics and statistical mechanics; it provides an exact mathematical treatment of a molecular feedback mechanism.

sections.title: Deciphering multiple binding modes in large protein complexes via Enhanced Sampling and beta-VAE: the CYFIP1-eIF4E case
sections.abstract: Enhanced molecular sampling and latent-space clustering are used to propose three binding modes for the flexible CYFIP1–eIF4E protein complex.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' simulations suggest CYFIP1 samples the canonical dorsal site, a non-canonical lateral site, and a combined mode on eIF4E, including contacts outside the previously emphasized interface.
sections.unique_caveat: The interface is computationally inferred. Coarse-graining and elastic-network restraints limit side-chain and large-scale motion, and under-sampled modes may be missed; direct mutagenesis or binding experiments remain necessary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New q-bio.BM submission, cross-listed in quantitative methods; ten enhanced-sampling replicas totaling 100 μs and recurring interface modes are method/relevance signals, not popularity evidence.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Two recurring directions in this selected corpus: function-aware protein and molecular-recognition evaluation (Confident and Wrong, CARVE, antibody masking); and computational models of gene response and regulation (S1Pert, exact stochastic RNA feedback theory). The evidence types differ and do not establish prospective validation.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Proposed follow-ups include testing function-guided selection across protein families and ligands, evaluating glycan poses on post-cutoff structures plus prospective assays, validating S1Pert predictions in new CRISPR contexts, experimentally testing RNA-feedback predictions, and assessing MRI reconstruction on prospective multi-site data.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The strongest directly experimental result is a bounded lanmodulin design comparison; other notable items include a sizable glycan benchmark, an accepted antibody-method revision, and computational gene-regulation and MRI work. This is a relevance-ranked shortlist, not a popularity chart or clinical evidence assessment.
